decision: Extract the mission/runtime reliability slice first from PR #25 onto the clean reliability base, and make coordinator mutations memory-transactional with exact rollback on persistence failure.

included: exact in-memory rollback when persistence fails
worker session fencing and restart recovery

reviews.preferred: snapshot-before-mutation plus exact rollback after save failure
reviews.reason: A failed durable mutation must not remain visible in coordinator memory after the caller receives an error; otherwise reads can observe state that never committed.

reviews.preferred: poison coordinator after persistence failure while restoring the last durable in-memory state
reviews.reason: Fail-closed prevents further mutations, and rollback avoids exposing uncommitted ownership, lease tokens, attempts or idempotency entries through read APIs.

reviews.preferred: in-memory snapshot rollback rather than reloading storage or adding a transactional database
reviews.reason: The extra structured clone is local and bounded by queue size, adds no network or Qubes latency, preserves the existing store format and has lower regression surface than introducing external transactional infrastructure.

alternatives.approach: leave mutated memory in place and only poison later writes
alternatives.rejectedBecause: read APIs can expose a mutation that the durable store rejected

alternatives.approach: reload from storage after a failed save
alternatives.rejectedBecause: adds failure-path I/O and creates a second failure mode if the store is unavailable or corrupt at the moment rollback is needed

alternatives.approach: move immediately to an external transactional database
alternatives.rejectedBecause: stronger multi-process atomicity is unnecessary for this dependency-root slice and would add latency, operational resources and migration risk

gates: atomic store load/save and corruption rejection
serialized coordinator persistence and fail-closed behavior
failed enqueue leaves no uncommitted mission or idempotency entry in memory
failed claim restores queued state, attempts and lease ownership exactly
request journal restart and command-substitution rejection
worker session fencing, retry and capability enforcement

failuresAndLessons: The first fail-closed coordinator design poisoned subsequent writes but did not roll back the mutation that failed persistence.
Process-restart restore semantics cannot be reused blindly for rollback because running work may be requeued; rollback needs an exact restore mode.
Reads after a persistence error are only safe if in-memory state matches the last durable snapshot.
lessons: Keep transport/Qubes semantics out of the dependency-root slice.
Do not treat a mergeable integration PR as independently release-ready.
A smaller slice is useful only if its original regression suite is retained rather than replaced.
Fail-closed must cover visibility of failed mutations, not only rejection of later writes.
